title: export_trace reports a source column's `origin` as the most-DOWNSTREAM carrier (usually the target node), not its true upstream origin
description:
In the `sources` section, the per-column origin is computed by iterating ALL steps and keeping the LAST step whose `output_values` contains the column:

    origin_node = None
    for s in steps:
        if col in s.output_values:
            origin_node = s.node_name
    sources.append({"column": col, ..., "origin": origin_node})

`output_values` is the FULL output row of each node (every column present at that node's output, including columns merely carried through), not just newly-added columns — confirmed at trace.py:833 `output_values=output_row` where `output_row` is the whole correlated row. Consequently `col` is present in the `output_values` of every step from the column's creation point all the way through to the traced target step. Because the loop overwrites `origin_node` on each match and does NOT break, it returns the LAST (most-downstream) step that still carries the column — which is the target node itself (or the final step), i.e. the OPPOSITE of an origin. The field is named `origin`, the module docstring describes `sources` as 'input columns and their origins', and the test `test_export_includes_input_sources` (test_trace_hero_tdd.py:796) documents the intent as 'Lists each input column and its origin node'. So the value returned is silently semantically wrong. A correct implementation would select the FIRST producing step (e.g. the first step where `col in s.schema_diff.columns_added`, or simply `break` on the first `output_values` match for upstream-most carrier).
evidence: _trace_export.py:62-66 keeps the LAST match (no break) over steps that are in pipeline order; trace.py:833 sets output_values to the full output row (carried-through columns included), so `col in s.output_values` is True for every downstream step including the target; the existing export_trace tests (test_trace_coverage.py:1017-1084, test_trace_hero_tdd.py:796-820) assert only the column NAMES in `sources`, never the `origin` value, so the defect is untested. Note also export_trace has no production caller (grep over src/ outside review/ shows only the definition; all other references are tests), which limits blast radius but the stated contract is still violated.
